1 

 Sandeep Sharma, Judge (oral):
Bail petitioner namely, Gurpal Singh, who is behind the bars since 17.03.2024, has approached this Court in the instant proceedings filed under Section 483 of Bharatiya Nagarik Suraksha Sanhita (hereinafter 'BNSS') praying therein for grant of regular bail in FIR No.07 of 2024, dated 12.03.2024, under Sections 376 and 506 of the Indian Penal Code, 1860 and Section 67-A of Information Technology Act, 2000 registered at Women Police Station, Dharamshala, District Kangra, Himachal Pradesh.

Whether the reporters of the local papers may be allowed to see the judgment?
2. Pursuant to the order dated 22.08.2024, respondent-State has filed status report and ASI Rita Kumari, I/O, .
Women P.S. Dharamshala, District Kangra, H.P has come present alongwith the record.
Record perused and returned.

3. Careful perusal of status report/record clearly reveals that on 30.08.2022, victim prosecutrix (name withheld to protect her identity) came present at Women Police Station, Dharamshala along with her mother for lodging the complaint against petitioner.
She alleged that few days back she had come in contact with the bail petitioner and since then they both had been meeting and talking with each other.

She alleged that petitioner called her at Ropar (Punjab) on the pretext that since they both have to solemnize marriage, she must come and see where does he work and he would also arrange some work for her at Ropar.
She alleged that when she reached Ropar, bail petitioner made her drink juice containing intoxicant, as a result thereof, she became unconscious.
She alleged that when she regained conscious, she found herself in naked condition.

She alleged that the bail petitioner made physical relations with her against her wishes and repeatedly compelled her to come to Ropar on the pretext that in case, she does not come to meet him, he would made her obscene photographs and videos viral.
She alleged that when she refused to meet him, he started sending obscene photographs and videos to her relatives, whose telephone numbers he had unauthorizedly taken from her mobile.

In the aforesaid .
background, FIR No.07/2024 dated 12.03.2024 came to be lodged against the petitioner.

Since,
challan stands filed in the competent court of law and nothing remains to be recovered from the bail petitioner, prayer has been made on behalf of the petitioner for grant of bail during the pendency of the trial.

4. While fairly admitting factum with regard to filing of Challan in the competent court of law, Mr.
B.C. Verma, learned Additional Advocate General, submits that though nothing remains to be recovered from bail petitioner, but keeping in view the gravity of offence alleged to have been committed by him, he does not deserve any leniency.

Mr. B.C. Verma, learned Additional Advocate General submits that there is overwhelming evidence available on record suggestive of the fact that Date Of Decision: 11.09.2024 vs State Of H.P on 11 September, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/171788620/
2 bail petitioner sexually assaulted victim prosecutrix against her wishes on the pretext of marriage and thereafter made her obscene videos, with a view to blackmail her in future.

Mr. B.C. Verma,
learned Additional Advocate General states that as per investigation bail petitioner uploaded obscene photographs and videos of victim prosecutrix on the phones of relatives of the victim prosecutrix, as a result thereof, she is not only facing trauma, but has suffered humiliation also.

Lastly, learned Additional Advocate General submits that since petitioner-accused has been booked under Section 376 IPC, prayer made on his behalf .
for grant of bail deserves out right rejection because in the event of his being enlarged on bail, he may not only flee from justice, but may again cause harm to the victim prosecutrix, whose statement is yet to be recorded in the competent court of law.
5. Having heard learned counsel representing the parties and perused material available on record,
especially statements of victim recorded under Section 161 and 164 of Cr.PC, this Court finds that two years prior to the date of lodging of FIR, victim prosecutrix had come in the contact of the bail petitioner and since then they both had been meeting and talking to each other.
It also emerges from the investigation that victim prosecutrix is major and when she started meeting bail petitioner, she was student of B.Sc Nursing.

Most importantly, it clearly emerges from the statement made by the victim prosecutrix that she of her own violation and without there any external pressure had been meeting bail petitioner and at no point of time, she was ever compelled by bail petitioner to join his company.

6. Having noticed conduct of the victim prosecutrix as apparent from her statements recorded under Section 161 and 164 of Cr.P.C, this Court is not persuaded to agree with Mr. B.C. Verma, learned Additional Advocate General, that bail petitioner took advantage of innocence of victim-prosecutrix,
rather it is quite .
apparent from the statements given by the victim-prosecutrix that since she wanted to solemnize marriage with the petitioner, she herself had been joining his company at Ropar.

Though, initially case under Section 67A of I.T. Act was registered against the petitioner , but since nothing obscene was found in the mobile of the bail petitioner, aforesaid provision of law was deleted and at present he stands charged under Section 376 of IPC.

7. Careful perusal of the status report reveals that learned Sessions Judge while considering prayer of the petitioner for grant of bail had no occasion to see video allegedly uploaded by the petitioner,
but even in such video, nothing was objectionable, save and except victim-prosecutrix and bail petitioner could be seen lying on one bed.
8.

Though, at this stage, Mr. B.C. Verma, learned Additional Advocate General attempted to argue that since case under Section 354D stands registered against petitioner apart from Section 376,.subsequent conduct of petitioner, whereby he uploaded the obscene photographs of the victim-prosecutrix on mobile phones of relatives of the victim prosecutrix does not entitle him to bail during the pendency of trial, however, this Court having perused provision under Section 354 (c) & (d) has no hesitation to conclude that both the aforesaid provisions are bailable and there is no Date Of Decision: 11.09.2024 vs State Of H.P on 11 September, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/171788620/
3 allegation, if any, .
of stalking, rather precise allegation as has been alleged by victim prosecutrix is that bail petitioner had been sexually assaulting her against her wishes on the pretext of marriage.
If it is so, case under Section 354 (c) & (d) may not be otherwise tenable against the petitioner.

9. Though the case at hand is to be decided by the Court below in totality of evidence collected on record by the prosecution, but keeping in view the aforesaid glaring aspect of the matter, coupled with the fact that petitioner is behind the bars for more than five months, there appears to be no justification to let bail petitioner incarcerate in jail for indefinite period during trial, especially when,
guilt, if any, of him is yet to be established on record.
10. Hon'ble Apex Court and this Court in a catena of cases have repeatedly held that one is deemed to be innocent, till the time, his/her is proved guilty in accordance with law.

Apprehension expressed by learned Additional Advocate General that in the event of bail petitioner being enlarged on bail, he may flee from justice, can be best met by putting him to stringent conditions.
11.
Needless to say, object of the bail is to secure the attendance of the accused in the trial and the proper test to be applied .
in the solution of the question whether bail should be granted or refused is whether it is probable that the party will appear to take his trial.
Otherwise, bail is not to be withheld as a punishment.
Otherwise also, normal rule is of bail and not jail.

Court has to keep in mind nature of accusations,
nature of evidence in support thereof, severity of the punishment which conviction will entail,
character of the accused, circumstances which are peculiar to the accused involved in that crime.

12. Hon'ble Apex Court in Criminal Appeal No. 227/2018, Dataram Singh vs. State of Uttar Pradesh & Anr decided on 6.2.2018 has held that freedom of an individual cannot be curtailed for indefinite period, especially when his/her guilt is yet to be proved.

entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text:
It has been further held by the Hon'ble Apex Court in the aforesaid judgment that a person is believed to be innocent until found guilty.
13.

Hon'ble Apex Court in Sanjay Chandra versus Central Bureau of Investigation (2012)1 Supreme Court Cases 49 has held that gravity alone cannot be a decisive ground to deny bail, rather competing factors are required to be balanced by the court while exercising its discretion.

The object of bail is neither punitive nor preventative.

4 be applied in the solution of the question whether bail should be granted or refused is whether it is probable that the party will appear to take his trial.

Apart from above, Court has to keep in mind nature of accusations, nature of evidence in support thereof, severity of the punishment, which conviction will entail, character of the accused,
circumstances which are peculiar to the accused involved in that crime.

15. The Apex Court in Prasanta Kumar Sarkar versus Ashis Chatterjee and another (2010) 14 SCC 496, has laid down various principles to be kept in mind, while deciding petition for bail viz. prima facie case, nature and gravity of accusation, punishment involved, apprehension of repetition of offence and witnesses being influenced.

sentences.text:
16. In view of the aforesaid discussion as well as law laid down by the Hon'ble Apex Court, petitioner has carved out a case for grant of bail, accordingly, the petition is allowed and the petitioner is ordered to be enlarged on bail in aforesaid FIR, subject to his furnishing bail bonds in the sum of Rs.2,00,000/- with two local .
sureties in the like amount each, to the satisfaction of the learned trial Court, besides the following conditions:
a.

He shall make himself available for the purpose of in- terrogation, if so required and regularly attend the trial Court on each and every date of hearing and if pre- vented by any reason to do so, seek exemption from appearance by filing appropriate application; b.

He shall not tamper with the prosecution evidence nor hamper the investigation of the case in any manner whatsoever;
c.

He shall not make any inducement, threat or promises to any person acquainted with the facts of the case so as to dissuade him/her from disclosing such facts to the Court or the Police Officer; and d.
He shall not leave the territory of India without the prior permission of the Court.
e. He shall surrender his passport, if any, before the in- vestigating agency.

17. It is clarified that if the petitioner misuses the liberty or violates any of the condition imposed upon him, the investigating agency shall be free to move this Court for cancellation of the bail.
18. Any observations made hereinabove shall not be construed to be a reflection on the merits of the case and shall remain confined to the disposal of this petition alone.
The petitions stand accordingly disposed of.

19. Learned counsel for the petitioner is permitted to produce copy of order downloaded from the High Court website before the concerned authority, who shall not insist for certified copy of the order, however, it may verify the order from the High Court website or otherwise.
